For 0<alpha<1 the only sensitive coefficients are c_n−tau*c_(n−m), and the exact ratio c_n/c_(n−m) is a product of m strictly increasing terms in n, whose minimum is c_(m+1)/c_1. The alpha=1 endpoint follows from an explicit three-term polynomial. Gamma asymptotics and exact nonconcavity value 151/551 are checked independently. Standard-library exact-rational finite diagnostics passed 41970 assertions; finite checks do not replace the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The problem is structural: normalized complete-Pick kernels are not preserved under Schur multiplication. The theorem characterizes exactly when a fractional Hardy factor survives one high-frequency sparse Pick factor, in a two-parameter power/order family; its sharp gamma-decaying boundary and first failing coefficient give a stability mechanism, while an explicit complete-Pick/nonconcave multiplier example separates two important operator geometries. No general paper-sized theorem is asserted.
